questions.source: Johnsy said, "I want to see the last leaf."
options: Johnsy said that she wanted to see the last leaf.
Johnsy said that I wanted to see the last leaf.
Johnsy said that she want to see the last leaf.
questions.rule: I becomes she and want moves back to wanted.

questions.source: Sue woke up. She saw Johnsy staring at the window.
options: When Sue woke up, she sees Johnsy staring at the window.
When Sue woke up when she saw Johnsy staring at the window.
When Sue woke up, she saw Johnsy staring at the window.
questions.rule: When begins the subordinate clause; the main clause keeps the past tense: she saw.

options: Behrman asked Sue why had she allowed such thoughts.

Behrman asked Sue why she had allowed such thoughts.
questions.rule: A reported question uses statement order (she had allowed) and ends with a full stop.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: Behrman had painted the leaf before the storm ended.
Behrman had paint the leaf before the storm ended.
Behrman has painted the leaf before the storm ended.
questions.rule: The earlier past action takes had + past participle: had painted.

chat: What did the doctor tell Sue?
options: He told to her that Johnsy had one chance in ten.
He told her that Johnsy had one chance in ten.
He told her that Johnsy has had one chance in ten.
questions.rule: told takes the person directly (no to), and has moves back to had.

chat: What would you do if you had a lot of money?
options: If I have a lot of money, I would build a hospital.
If I had a lot of money, I would build a hospital.
If I had a lot of money, I will build a hospital.
questions.rule: Type 2 (imagined): If + simple past, would + base verb.

questions.source: The last leaf fell. Behrman painted a new one on the wall.
options: After the last leaf had fallen, Behrman painted a new one on the wall.
After the last leaf has fallen, Behrman painted a new one on the wall.
After the last leaf had fell, Behrman painted a new one on the wall.
questions.rule: The earlier action takes the past perfect: had fallen. After had, use the participle fallen, not fell.

options: Behrman was a painter who lived on the ground floor.
Behrman was a painter which lived on the ground floor.
Behrman was a painter who live on the ground floor.
questions.rule: For a person, use who; the past story needs lived.

options: He was absent because of he had a fever.
He was absent because he had a fever.
He was absent because he have a fever.

chat: Will you come to the art show on Sunday?
options: Yes, if I finish my project, I will come.
Yes, if I will finish my project, I will come.
Yes, if I finish my project, I would came.
questions.rule: Type 1: if + simple present (finish), will + base verb (come).

questions.source: Sue said to Johnsy, "Try to sleep."
options: Sue told Johnsy try to sleep.
Sue told Johnsy that to try to sleep.
Sue told Johnsy to try to sleep.
questions.rule: A command becomes told + person + to + verb: told Johnsy to try.

options: The leaf had been painted by Behrman during the storm.
The leaf had painted by Behrman during the storm.

questions.rule: Past perfect passive = had been + past participle: had been painted.

options: If I was you, I will rest for a week.

chat: Why were you so sleepy at breakfast?
options: I had been studying till midnight.
I had been study till midnight.
I have been studying till midnight yesterday.
questions.rule: A long action up to a past moment: had been + verb-ing.

chat: Neha, what did Vikram say on the phone?
options: He said me that he would come to school the next day.
He said that he will come to school the next day.
He said that he would come to school the next day.
questions.rule: After said, will becomes would. Use told me or said, not said me.

questions.source: If you do not take your medicine, you will not get well.
options: Unless you do not take your medicine, you will not get well.
Unless you take your medicine, you will not get well.
Unless you will take your medicine, you will not get well.
questions.rule: Unless already means if not, so drop do not; no will after unless.

The leaf that Johnsy saw had been painted by the old man who lived downstairs.

chat: Why did Ananya miss the final?
options: She has injured her ankle the day before, so she could not play.
She had injured her ankle the day before, so she could not play.
She had injured her ankle the day before, so she cannot played.
questions.rule: the day before is earlier than the past match: had injured; then could not + base verb.

questions.source: Johnsy said to Sue, "Will you open the window?"
options: Johnsy asked Sue if she will open the window.
Johnsy asked Sue if she would open the window.
Johnsy asked Sue if would she open the window.
questions.rule: said to becomes asked, will becomes would, and statement order: if she would.

questions.prompt: Rewrite as one sentence beginning with 'If'.

options: If Johnsy were strong, she could fight the illness.
If Johnsy is strong, she could fight the illness.
If Johnsy were strong, she can fight the illness.
questions.rule: An unreal present takes type 2: If + were, then could + base verb.
